stemMd: An engineering firm argues that documenting failed prototypes will prevent repeated design errors in later projects. Which finding most strengthens its argument?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The firm has developed successful prototypes too.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Later teams often repeat failures already encountered elsewhere in the firm but are unaware of those earlier attempts.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Each team uses a different project name.

explanationMd: The finding identifies exactly the information failure the proposal could remedy: prior relevant lessons exist but do not reach later teams.

distractorRationale.d: Storage capability is not evidence of the proposed knowledge gap.
distractorRationale.e: Naming differences do not demonstrate causal repetition.
distractorRationale.a: Successes do not establish whether failure documentation addresses repetition.
distractorRationale.c: Expense alone does not show that documentation changes future choices.
